anchor.problem: Multi-corner (MCMM) static timing analysis cost grows with the number of declared scenarios, and existing reductions save runtime only by skipping scenarios on estimated, empirical, learned or experience-based criteria that cannot guarantee zero missed violations.
anchor.engineering_user: Timing-closure and signoff engineers (and closure-flow owners) who must obtain timing decisions at every scenario of a declared scenario set during closure iterations and before signoff.
anchor.downstream_need: The complete decision set of full MCMM analysis of the declared scenario set: every violating (endpoint, scenario, check) triple, exact slacks below a reporting margin M, and WNS/TNS per scenario. It must come with zero missed violations relative to full analysis and with lower end-to-end turnaround.
anchor.causal_mechanism: Per scenario, an exact clock-network pass plus a cheap data-network bound pass. The bound pass uses only that scenario's own characterized tables and parasitics, and its bounds are sound with respect to the reference engine's delay-calculation semantics. Together they certify (endpoint, scenario, check) triples whose slack lower bound clears M. Exact analysis is then restricted to the fan-in cones of uncertified triples. Decisions equal full analysis by construction; runtime falls because most triples in non-dominant scenarios have margins larger than the bound band.
mechanism_invariants: Zero missed violations relative to full reference analysis of the declared scenario set, by construction under audited soundness properties; never by estimation, calibration or learning
Exact slack values for every reported triple below the margin M, plus exact WNS/TNS when negative
No parametric, monotone-in-PVT or learned cross-scenario model; each scenario is bounded from its own characterized data
Evaluation against the strongest full-MCMM baseline (all scenarios in one pinned OpenSTA run) under equal resources
One pinned reference engine and delay calculator define soundness; any new calculator needs its own audit
forbidden_pivots: Replacing the mechanism with a straightforward combination of prior methods
Optimizing a proxy without a demonstrated engineering need
Changing the user or downstream objective to avoid a valid objection
Replacing sound certificates with estimated cutoffs, learned predictors or calibrated safety margins while keeping a guarantee claim
Dropping exact refinement and reporting only bounds as if they were slacks
Redefining success as average slack error or correlation instead of decision equivalence
Attributing speedup to parallelism or hardware scaling rather than to certification
